overlap_notes: I grade W1-04-r4. Overlap on docs/shots/ and reports/blog-feed.jsonl is the project's whole method and is shared by every live piece; the feed is append-only and I appended one line and edited nobody else's. I wrote no game/ source.

findings.AGGREGATION_FAILS_AND_WHY: tools/world/w1-04-consumption.mjs, run end to end (RULES.md rule 9), exits 1: 19/20 CONSUMED, one DEAD. The DEAD row is 10a, the check the builder edited: exterior_restored_on_exit reads 105 against a pass condition of 115. ATTRIBUTED door by door: the check takes the street signature BEFORE opening the door - i.e. wherever the previous door's exit left the body - and requires it back after leaving THIS door, so it fails at every town boundary. 4 of 4 failures in my 32-door replication are settlement changes, all with room_was_drawn true and room_differs_from_street true. The BUILD is fine; the CHECK is mis-specified, and its author has never seen its output.
findings.DOORSTEP_INSIDE_THE_BUILDING: THE BIGGEST GAP. buildings[].door sits at the building CENTRE on 112 of 112 (max door-to-centre distance 0.00 m); every declared continuity.exterior_spawn falls inside its own building's wall box; live, through exitInterior() and buildingAt(), 39 of 40 doors tested leave the player inside the building they just left, 35 by more than a metre. Round 4's correct roof fix closes the lid. Photographed.
findings.LAMPS_OUTSIDE: 55 authored lamps in 19 of the 41 shrunk rooms now stand outside their own room's bounds; 12 are non-snuffable hearths; worst 2.33 m out; 0 in any room the join did not shrink. buildInterior() and sim/stealth/system.js#syncInteriorLights() both place them at the record's verbatim pos, so the Souls-side detection model reads lights that are outside the rooms they light. applyInteriorBounds() already clamps continuity.interior_spawn for exactly this reason.
findings.MESHES_OUTSIDE: 292 built meshes in 63 rooms stand more than 0.6 m outside their own room's bounds - 179 light fittings and 113 props. 218 across 26 rooms are in the 41 rooms the join shrank; 74 across 37 rooms are pre-existing slot looseness.
findings.SIGNATURE_SURVIVES: getDrawnSignature() passed every degenerate case. Live: empty scene 0 meshes / hash of nothing; the same room at 0/2/60/600 fixed steps = ONE hash (the pixel sweep gave 8 of 8 distinct after 2 steps in this same room); two camera poses = 1; positive control separates street/room/other room 3 of 3. Offline algebra: same content twice = 1, root moved 4 km = 1, children reordered = 1, mesh removed changes it, 1 cm move changes it, name change changes it. Scope limits: it counts meshes that are visible:false, and it is blind to lighting and to non-colour material properties - both conservative for a distinctness claim.
findings.OFFLINE_EQUALS_LIVE: The builder's own stated open question is CLOSED: archon-apothecary is cc6a50ac / 114 meshes offline and cc6a50ac / 114 meshes live; blackrose-inn is 33400225 both sides. The offline room is the room the player is standing in, so the offline 115-room count is admissible evidence about the drawn world.
findings.CONFIRMED_JOIN: 41 -> 0 reproduces independently in bare Node; worst area ratio 1.0887; 41 rooms limited; worst archon-market keeping 0.1714.
findings.CONFIRMED_ROOFS: 0 of 202 by my own 8x8 downward raycast above half wall height, worst coverage 1.000; the instrument goes red at 201 of 202 when every mesh above half height is scaled 0.7 in plan (rule 4).
findings.CONFIRMED_BY_REFERENCE: sim/npc.js#anchorFor() reads d.bounds_m and applyInteriorBounds() mutates the same objects; the 1.2 m inset never exceeds a half-extent (smallest joined room 4.34 x 10.94 m, 0 of 115 collapse). Unique items follow the shrink 115 of 115.
findings.CONFIRMED_NULLING_GONE: api.js __w1_04_perturbSettlement no longer nulls _townCell behind _settleSettlementSolids()'s back.
findings.TAUTOLOGY_TRUE_BUT_NOT_NEW: bounds_m equals continuity.exterior_footprint_m on 115 of 115, so any N1 ratio dividing one by the other is 1.000 by construction. True - and first stated by the round-3 critic. Round 4's contribution is measuring it off the built scene graph so the ratio can fail, which is the harder half.
findings.DEEP_OVERLAPS_BOUNDARY: The shipped tool reports 12; the identical formula without its +1e-6 epsilon reports 14. Two pairs sit exactly on the 45% line.
findings.SMALLEST_ROOM_SPAN: The 2x2 table's 4.64 m is the built shell's outer extent; bounds_m - what npc.js, the spawn clamp and every prop slot are placed against - is 4.34 m (MIN_ENTERABLE_SPAN_M 5.0 minus ROOM_INSET_M 0.66) in eight rooms. Both right, different quantities.

not_done_stated_plainly: The uncapped 115-room LIVE distinctness sweep. I ran 32 doors live for the L1 attribution and 40 for L6; my first attempt at the full 115 died inside one page.evaluate exactly as the builder's did. Mitigated rather than excused: the offline and live signatures are byte-identical for the same room, so the offline 115 is evidence about the drawn world.

The formal L5 degradation check (delete getDrawnSignature and watch 10a go DEAD). The browser hung on the section before it and I killed it. The code path is unambiguous by reading and I state it in the verdict as a reading, not a measurement.

RI-WLD03 M13, the blind top-down layout test - rule 25 binds me exactly as it bound the builder, because I took the top-down capture M13 needs. Three rounds have now deferred it for the same correct reason; it needs its own dispatch.
inCoverFraction on both arms of the town collision set - untouched for a third round, and more urgent now that 19 rooms' lamp positions are wrong.
The observed-theft branch - untouched for a third round.

Two pictures: a clean street-level shot of the Blackrose terraces (my surveyed standing points controlled for building walls and not for canopy props) and the inside of archon-market (refused three times by the capture daemon's settle gate on interior ambient motion).
No timing figure is published anywhere in this verdict (rule 26).
method_deviations: node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned GO at every check I made. One browser for the live arm, launched once and kept; all pictures went through the pooled capture daemon and launched nothing.

I killed my own stalled live run with `pkill -f headless_shell`, which is not scoped to my process and may have taken a neighbour's browser with it. Careless, reported rather than hidden (rule 26). Browsers were running again within thirty seconds; every later kill was by my own PID.

My first live instrument ran all 115 doors inside one page.evaluate with no intermediate write and outlived its wrapper - the same wall the builder reported. Restructured to chunk in eights and save after each chunk (rule 2), which is the only reason the L1 attribution survived.

MY OWN PROBE DEFECTS, all three reported in the verdict: (1) my first offline census called buildInterior(rec) instead of buildInterior(root, rec), traversed 0 meshes in 115 of 115 rooms and reported a clean 'nothing outside the room'; rule 4 caught it and the fixed run gives the opposite answer. (2) I read whereAmI().door instead of .door_in_reach and briefly had 'you cannot get back in', which I do not claim. (3) My 'people in the room' arm recorded npcs_in_sim: 0 and proves nothing about moving bodies.
I did not re-run the builder's own probes except once - w1-04-r3-exterior.mjs --offline - deliberately, to compare its residual_deep_overlaps with my own formula, which is how the epsilon surfaced.
